before_fix_numbers.growth_pattern: exponential/quadratic - CTX climbed 99% -> 117% -> 162% -> 807.6% -> 1088.2% within minutes while real promptTokens per finish-step event stayed in the tens of thousands

after_fix_numbers.growth_pattern: linear/sane - CTX grew 16% -> 20% -> 22% -> 24% over ~2 minutes, matching real conversation growth. promptTokens from the raw event log (agent-events.jsonl) confirm: 41913 -> 43315 -> 43826 -> 43904 -> 44574, small monotonic increments consistent with a real growing conversation, NOT the exponential blow-up seen before the fix.

residual_secondary_note: The displayed CTX% (22-24%) matches promptTokens/200000, NOT promptTokens/128000 -- the swarm/tokens observability panel's contextWindowLimit is set once per agent via observability.ts:253 `getModelContextWindow(meta?.model ?? 'default')`, where `model` comes from task metadata (a shorthand like 'sonnet' or the literal string 'default'), NOT the resolved router-prefixed id ('glm/glm-5') that the actual session/runner.ts safety guard uses. This means the UI's percentage is still off by the 200k-vs-128k denominator (a DIFFERENT, smaller instance of the same root pattern, in a DIFFERENT call site), but the CRITICAL bug asked about here -- the quadratic/exponential ACCUMULATION bug in stream-handler.ts -- is conclusively fixed: the displayed numbers now track the real, linearly-growing conversation size instead of exploding past 1000%. This residual denominator mismatch was NOT part of the original fix scope and was not corrected in this session; flagged honestly as a further, smaller finding rather than folded into the verified-fix claim.
verdict: END-TO-END VERIFIED. The quadratic-accumulation fix in stream-handler.ts holds up under a real multi-step agentic session driven through the real TUI against the live router, with the rebuilt worker bundle. This is not a unit check -- it is the same standard of proof as the primary models.ts fix.
unplanned_bonus_finding_this_run: The auth check ('Authentication required') that blocked starting this re-drive on the first two attempts was traced to a stray APERANT_USER_DATA=/tmp/aperant-userdata-pp environment variable leaked into the driving Python kernel's os.environ from an earlier, unrelated investigation. tuistory_drive.py's _run() forwards the FULL current process environment to every `tuistory launch` call, so this stray var silently redirected app.getPath('userData') away from the real ~/.aperant for every relaunch until it was found and unset. This was a harness/environment-hygiene issue in the verification session, not a defect in aperant-tui's own code.
